questions.explanation: Relation: antonym (the two words are opposites). Ancient → Modern, so Victory → Defeat. 'Success' means nearly the same as victory, not the opposite.
Relation: part-whole (the first is a part of the second). Finger → Hand, so Toe → Foot. A nail is part of the toe: the relation the wrong way round.
Relation: tool-user (the first is a tool used by the second). Stethoscope → Doctor, so Brush → Painter. Canvas and paint are what the brush is used on or with, not the person who uses it.
Relation: category-member (the second is a member of the first category). Metal → Iron, so Colour → Blue. A rainbow contains colours but isn't one; 'bright' describes a colour.
Relation: sequence (the second comes right after the first). Monday → Tuesday, so March → April. February comes before March and May two months after; only April comes straight after.
Relation: degree (the second is a stronger form of the first). Warm → Hot, so Cool → Cold. Ice and winter are cold things, not a stronger word for 'cool'.
Relation: synonym (the two words mean the same). Brief → Short, so Vast → Huge. An ocean is vast, but it is an example, not a word with the same meaning.
Relation: function (the first is used for the second). Refrigerator → Cool, so Oven → Bake. Bread is what gets baked and a kitchen is where the oven is; neither is what the oven does.
Relation: part-whole (the first is a part of the second). Brick → Wall, so Link → Chain. Metal is what a link is made of (material), not the whole it is part of.
Relation: antonym (the two words are opposites). Generous → Stingy, so Cautious → Reckless. 'Careful' is a synonym of cautious; the opposite is reckless.

Relation: tool-user (the first is a tool used by the second). Baton → Conductor, so Scalpel → Surgeon. The patient is who the scalpel is used on, and an operation is what it is used for; the user is the surgeon.
Relation: cause-effect (the first causes the second). Overeating → Obesity, so Insomnia → Fatigue. Insomnia (not being able to sleep) leads to fatigue; the other options are only linked to sleep.
Relation: antonym (the two words are opposites). Conceal → Reveal, so Scatter → Gather. 'Spread' is close to scatter, and 'hide' copies the first pair's word; the opposite of scatter is gather.

Relation: degree (the second is a stronger form of the first). Nibble → Devour, so Glance → Stare. 'Look' is the neutral word; a stare is the long, intense form of a glance, as devouring is of nibbling.

Relation: function (the first is used for the second). Ruler → Length, so Clock → Time. A ruler measures length, a clock measures time. An hour is a unit of time (like a centimetre), and a watch is another clock.
